calls.head: The Bruins will hunt a mismatch
calls.body: At home, the Bruins have sent Peterka’s line (Peterka, Khusnutdinov and Minten) out against opponents’ third lines 41% of the time, when no line matching would give about 27%. That’s Marco Sturm chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Flyers’ third line is Bunting, Acciari and Cates.
calls.call: The Bruins’ L2 (Peterka, Khusnutdinov and Minten) spends at least 41% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flyers’ third line.
calls.cite: Who plays against whom · Boston home games this season · 3 games, 31 minutes for this group at 5-on-5
calls.happened: Boston’s L2 (Peterka, Khusnutdinov, Minten) spent 84% of its 5-on-5 time against Philadelphia’s L3 (4:05 of 4:51), against a home habit of 41% and about 27% with no line matching.

calls.head: In close against from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Philadelphia ranks 16th in the league and Boston ranks 29th. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Flyers take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Bruins.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 5 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shots from within 20 feet, Philadelphia had 27% and Boston 21%. Coming in, Philadelphia was at 31% and Boston at 29%.

BOS.head: We had this close to even (47% for Boston), and Boston came through.

PHI.head: We had this close to even (53% for Philadelphia), and it went Boston’s way.

surprises.head: Boston buried Philadelphia in shots
surprises.body: Boston took 70% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Boston would expect about 55%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Philadelphia leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Philadelphia’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 43% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

story.head: The Bruins roll past the Flyers
paras: Pavel Zacha opened the scoring midway through the first. Five different Bruins scored.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Bruins win nine in ten. By our Swing measure, Fraser Minten had the best night of anyone.

items.text: The Flyers haven’t won in six.
Pavel Zacha scored his first goal of the season.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
